idea: Executive education modules on real assets and the built environment
buyer: Business schools, professional bodies, corporate L&D
pain: Real assets teaching is either finance without buildings or buildings without finance
verdict: Good fees per delivery and a real curriculum gap, but institutional buying cycles are glacial.

why.distribution: Universities and professional bodies are not her network; entry is through committees.
why.demand: Exec ed budgets exist and modules are commissioned.
why.fmf: Almost nobody can teach both the finance and the buildings credibly.
why.revenue_structure: Repeat deliveries once a module is on a programme, without contract.
why.defensibility: Once embedded in a curriculum, modules persist for years.
why.ceiling: £11k x 18 deliveries = £198k, and eighteen two-day deliveries is a full year of teaching.

ceiling_arithmetic: £11k x 18 deliveries = £198k, requiring eighteen two-day teaching engagements - more than full-time part-time. Realistic: 4-6 = £44-66k.
carries: A genuine curriculum gap she is unusually qualified to fill, with materials that reuse.
kills: Institutional sales cycles measured in academic years, into committees she has no route to.
test: Approach two business schools and one professional body about a module.
test_pass: One puts it into a programme committee.
test_fail: No response, or a two-year timeline.
